_README: Machine-readable ledger of client-model fidelity GAPS. Each language key maps to a list of JSON paths (dot notation; '*' = any array index) that the client's Expectation model currently DROPS or MUTATES on a JSON round-trip, so its round-trip fidelity test can excuse exactly those paths and land green today. This file is the backlog for the model-completion wave: when a client model is fixed to carry a field, REMOVE its path here and the per-client test's ratchet re-arms the assertion (a stale entry that no longer excuses any diff fails CI). Keys beginning with '_' are metadata and are ignored by tests. See .opencode (roundtrip-spec) / the per-client test headers for the exact comparator algorithm. php has verbatim rawData replay, so it has zero gaps. NOTE: 'node' entries document the generated mockServer.d.ts TYPE gaps enforced at compile time via isolated // @ts-expect-error markers in test/roundtrip_fidelity_types.ts (the type test does NOT read this file); removing a .d.ts gap makes its marker unused and fails tsc. 'php' is empty because the PHP client replays decoded JSON verbatim. THIRD CATEGORY: a few entries are listed under '_representation-only' as well as under their language. Those are NOT defects and MUST NOT be 'fixed' by making the client preserve the input byte-for-byte: the client normalises the value to a different but semantically identical wire form, matching the Java reference's shortest-round-tripping-form rule. They stay in the language list because the ratchet needs them to excuse a real diff; preserving representation instead would diverge from Java.

_representation-only.httpRequest.headers.X-Negated.*: go: {"not":true,"value":"forbidden"} is re-emitted as "!forbidden". Both parse to not=true value=forbidden, and "!forbidden" is itself a fixed point, so this is the shortest round-tripping form -- the same choice the Java NottableString serializer makes. Semantically identical, verified against a live server; not a dropped or mutated value.

_notation: segment.segment ; array index as a literal index in a diff but written as '*' here so entries are fixture-length independent. A shorter entry excuses its whole subtree.
_go_note: httpRequest.pathParameters is a pre-existing model limitation, not a droppable field: HttpRequest.PathParametersList is typed map[string][]string and the public builder RequestBuilder.PathParameter(name string, values ...string) writes into it, but the schema-matcher wire form is { name: [ { schema: {...} } ] }, which []string cannot hold. Widening the field (or the builder) to carry schema objects is a breaking type/signature change, disallowed by the additive-only contract, so this one path is retained. All other go gaps were closed by additively adding typed fields. STILL ACCURATE after the matcher-value work: PathParameterMatchers carries the nottable object form (not/optional/value), NOT the schema matcher form ({schema:{...}}) this entry is about, so this gap is unchanged and the ratchet correctly still requires it.
_nottable_object_form_note: WHY (not an oversight, a deliberate deferral): a matcher value whose first character is '!' or '?' cannot be sent as a bare JSON string, because the receiver reads those characters as the negation / optional markers and strips them — so "path IS !foo" would arrive as "path is NOT foo". Such values are therefore sent in the NottableString OBJECT form ({"not":false,"value":"!foo"}), which the server reads verbatim and which the published stringOrJsonSchema has always permitted. matcher_request_literal_not.json is the probe, and the ledger entry is SCOPED to it (<unrepresentable-expectation>:matcher_request_literal_not) so a second fixture becoming unparseable is NOT silently excused by this entry. node, python and ruby accept the object form because their matcher fields are dynamically typed. go models path/method/header values as string (and so DROPS them); rust models them as Option<String> and dotnet as string, and BOTH hard-fail deserialization of the whole expectation rather than dropping one field. In practice that is worse than one expectation: retrieveActiveExpectations() deserializes a LIST, so a SINGLE object-form expectation created by a Java or Node user poisons the ENTIRE retrieve for every Rust and .NET consumer, not just the offending entry. Still preferable to the silent inversion it replaces — a hard failure is diagnosable — but the blast radius is the whole call. Closing this requires a NottableString UNION field type (string | object) in the go, rust and dotnet models. That is a breaking change to the type of a public field, which the additive-only client contract forbids, so it is recorded here rather than done silently — it needs its own major-version change. Note the failure mode is loud, not silent: before, such a value was inverted and looked correct; now it is rejected and is diagnosable. UPDATE (go): the claim above that closing this needs a breaking UNION field type, and therefore a major version, is DISPROVED for go and the entry is now scoped to path/method only. Header, query parameter, cookie and path-parameter VALUES are carried additively: the plain map fields keep their types and meanings, and parallel *Matchers fields (HeaderMatchers, QueryStringParameterMatchers, CookieMatchers, PathParameterMatchers) hold MatcherValue, with a custom MarshalJSON/UnmarshalJSON on HttpRequest letting the matcher map stand in for the plain one under the SAME wire key. No public field changed type, so no major version was needed. The same shape is available to rust (a manual Serialize impl, since serde offers no way for one field's skip_serializing_if to consult a sibling) and to dotnet (a JsonConverter<HttpRequest>). go's path/method remain gaps only because they are top-level scalars rather than maps; note they are also unreachable in practice, since a real request path starts with '/' and '!GET' is not a valid method token. IMPORTANT for whoever does rust/dotnet: the READ half is not optional. Without UnmarshalJSON the escape is write-only and retrieveActiveExpectations fails to decode the client's OWN output; and a nested UnmarshalJSON that returns an error makes encoding/json abort the PARENT decode, silently dropping httpResponse, so the path/method type mismatch must be tolerated while every other mismatch still propagates.
_action_field_gaps_note: WHY (straightforward, just out of scope for the unit that added the probes): these are fields the server schema declares and the client model does not carry, so they are dropped on a round-trip. Unlike the nottable gaps below they need NO field-type change — they are purely ADDITIVE model additions, so they are compatible with the additive-only client contract and can be closed at any time. Remaining: the streaming-action fields (httpSseResponse.templateType, httpWebSocketResponse.templateType and .graphqlSubscriptionFilter) missing from python, ruby, go and dotnet; and httpResponse.generateFromSchema / recoverAfter / statusCodeRange missing from various clients. These stay recorded because they are differently-shaped fields across several clients, not a single defect class. NOTE two entries that WERE in this list have been CLOSED rather than deleted silently: the `primary` action-selector flag (rust, go, dotnet) and `httpError.streamError` (rust, dotnet). Both were fixed because leaving an identical data-loss defect recorded in some clients while fixed in others is incoherent — `primary` selects which action runs when several are configured, so dropping it can silently change behaviour on re-submit. All of these were invisible until the fixture coverage gate was deepened below depth-0; graphqlSubscriptionFilter was expressible by ZERO clients including Java until rust gained it.
_nottable_marker_in_names_note: NOT FIXED, and not fixable the same way — header / query-parameter / cookie NAMES. The object-form fix described above applies to matcher VALUES only. A name is serialised as a JSON field name (KeysToMultiValuesSerializer writes it via jgen.writeFieldName, CookiesSerializer likewise), and a JSON field name is a string by construction — it cannot carry {"not":false,"value":...}. So header(string("!X-Foo", false), "bar") still serialises the NAME as bare "!X-Foo" and the receiver reads it as NOT X-Foo: the identical inversion, still live. This is PRE-EXISTING and was not introduced by the value fix. Closing it needs a schema change — keyToMultiValue.json's array form types `name` as a plain string, so the fix is to allow the object form there and teach the key serialisers/deserialisers to use it, across all 8 clients. That is a wire-format change of the same class as the value fix but with a larger blast radius, so it is recorded here rather than bundled in. No fixture probes it deliberately: adding one would fail every client at once for a defect none of them can currently express.
